gaps: P0: nothing. P5: nothing reliably dated (#29 is a 1915 negative of the 1890s photochrom #27; #25 dated only 1900–18; Hammond slide #30 undated, and its skyline may show St. Peter’s spire rebuilt in 1973).
notes: #2 Commons says 1572, but the Riga plate (with Königsberg) is in vol. 3, so 1581. P1 alternative: Thum and Mollyn’s 1612 panorama (#8, or the large dark CC0 scan #7), a true view printed in Riga, black and white. #14 is signed ‘fait par Aveline’; its caption says Sweden still holds Riga, so it predates 1710 (Commons gives 1710); decorative and probably derived from older views, so weaker. Merian’s bird’s-eye plan (#6, #9, #10) is dated 1638–1652 in different copies, so not used for P2. #18 is small (1200×415); its date comes from the file title. P3 alternative: 1830 lithograph of the Town Hall Square with the Blackheads’ House and St. Peter’s (#15, black and white, large). Sieges and the 1701 river crossing (#11, #13, #19, #20) skipped as event views.
